audit.why: Azir's Conquering Sands is 740 range vs Kassadin's 650 Q, and Arise! soldiers let him farm and poke without stepping up, so he owns Levels 3-5. Level 6 Riftwalk (5/3.5/2s) makes the stage genuinely even; first item flips it to Kassadin.

audit.why: Spike structure is right: Azir peaks 3-5, Kassadin at 6, first item, and 16.

audit.why: Shifting Sands is 22/20.5/19/17.5/16s and carries a shield; Emperor's Divide is 120/105/90s and creates terrain that blocks Riftwalk paths. Kassadin's Q interrupts channels and shields magic damage, which is all Azir deals.

edits.before: E joins once spells fly — the slow wave covers your farm walks. Still: survive, stack, smile.
edits.after: Force Pulse charges off his casts, but his 740-range Q still farms you out. Survive, stack, smile.

edits.before: W-refund farming keeps mana honest — take what's free, shield what isn't, and watch the clock.
edits.after: Nether Blade refunds keep mana honest, but his 740-range Q outranges your 650 — take what's free.

edits.before: First item spike: blink-strings start chunking. Take the trades you spent five levels refusing.
edits.after: First item: blink in while Shifting Sands is down 19s — take the trades you have refused all lane.

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. It governs your forward steps. - R Riftwalk spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Shifting Sands is down 22s at rank 1 and 16s at rank 5 — that gap is your only safe step forward. - Emperor's Divide is a 120s ultimate at rank 1; once he burns it, commit through the soldiers. - Riftwalk spent on poke is a death you scheduled.

edits.before: Q-shield his key spell, W refund the auto, walk — pre-6 trades are accounting; post-6 add a blink and they're arguments you win.
edits.after: Nether Blade's 7s cooldown refunds mana on each empowered last hit — farm with it so your Q shield is always affordable for his poke.

edits.before: Trading like the late game already arrived — a level 5 Kassadin with ambitions is a gold bounty with a shield.
edits.after: Before two items, stepping into Conquering Sands and Arise! soldier autos just hands him a bounty with a small shield.

edits.before: Azir wins by landing Shifting Sands, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Azir wins by shoving with soldiers, poking at 740 range, and walling your Riftwalk off with Emperor's Divide.

edits.before: Carry through inevitability — no champion converts time into power like Kassadin; your job is making the clock run.
edits.after: Carry by outliving his poke: Azir's damage is magic, your passive cuts it, and every wave farmed is a level closer to 16.

edits.before: Q-shield his key spell, W refund the auto, walk — pre-6 trades are accounting; post-6 add a blink and they're arguments you win.
edits.after: Q-shield the Conquering Sands wave, W-reset an auto on him, walk before soldiers re-arm — post-6 add a blink and you win it.

edits.before: Ahead, accelerate the clock: blink-trade Azir's every gap, follow each roam instantly, and reach three items before the map adjusts.
edits.after: Ahead, deny him stacks: blink onto Azir whenever Shifting Sands is down, take the soldier-free window, and hit three items early.
